evidence.quote:
Enhancement of pool boiling heat transfer in water by means of the introduction of free particles on the
heated surface is investigated.

High-speed visualizations show
that bubble nucleation preferentially occurs at the narrow corner cavities formed between the free particles and the heated surface.
An insulated copper heating block forms the base of a sealed liquid bath test chamber.

A uniform heat flux is
supplied to the test surface through 12 cartridge heaters embedded
in the copper block

At each heat flux, steady-state conditions are considered to have been reached when the time-averaged variation of
the wall superheat temperature, acquired every 3 s, is less than
0.0003 C/s for 150 s.

To perform a test, the tank is filled with 45 ml of water, and the
water is boiled for two hours

it is concluded that
3 mm to 6 mm particles are optimum when water is used as the
working fluid.

The polished (RRMS = 25 nm, NewView
6200, Zygo Corp.) top 25.4 mm 25.4 mm test surface of the heat-
ing block is exposed to the working fluid.

resulting in an average increase in heat transfer coefficient of 115% relative
to a baseline polished surface without particles

The layer of loose particles on the heated surface is free to move and
deform under the action of bulk liquid convection and vapor nucleation.

This technique introduces free-standing metal particles,
which may be orders of magnitude larger than nanoparticles, on
an immersed boiling surface.
